--- title: RevBayes and BEAST2 comparison subtitle: Fossilized birth-death and stratigraphic range models on the 5 ms song sequences author: Marcelo Araya-Salas date: "2026-11-13" toc: true toc-depth: 2 toc-location: left number-sections: true highlight-style: pygments execute: freeze: auto format: html: df-print: kable code-fold: true code-tools: true editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- ::: {.cell} :::
# Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted} Evaluate BEAST2 as an option for modelling song evolution, by asking two questions on two leks (HC1 and BR1): 1. Does BEAST2 give the same results as RevBayes under the same model? This is tested with the `bounds` and `all` datasets 2. Does treating the first and last year of a song type as a stratigraphic range change the results? This is tested with the `bounds` dataset, which has the first and last year of each song type 3. Do marginal likelihoods computed from BEAST2 runs lead to the same clock model choice (global vs relaxed) as RevBayes?
 
# Bottom line {.unnumbered .unlisted} - **BEAST2 reproduces RevBayes** under the same model (fossilized birth-death with sampled ancestors): the same parameters, trees, priors and clock model choice, in both leks and with both datasets - **sRanges is a different model, not a different program**: it changes little in HC1, but in BR1 it changes the support of several clades of song types and raises the song loss rate almost three-fold. Since RevBayes and BEAST2 SA agree, the change comes from modelling song types as ranges - **sRanges is not mature enough to rely on alone**: an early version with fewer tree moves than SA, and its fit to the data has not been tested yet - **Recommendation**: keep RevBayes for the main analyses, as in the first version, and use BEAST2 as an independent check. sRanges could be a sensitivity analysis, after testing its fit and tree moves (see [Summary](#summary))
  # Load packages {.unnumbered .unlisted} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sketchy::load_packages(packages = c("knitr", "ggplot2", "ape", "coda")) theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 13)) knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, dpi = 120, fig.retina = 1) leks <- c("HC1", "BR1") rb_dir <- "./output/pilot_5ms" bt_dir <- "./output/pilot_5ms/beast2" burnin <- 0.1 # discarded from the start of BEAST2 runs. RevBayes runs have a separate burn-in stage n_trees <- 1500 # trees per run used to compare clades models <- c("RevBayes FBD", "BEAST2 SA", "BEAST2 sRanges") ``` ::: # The models All models use the same data for each lek: the `bounds` dataset aligned with MAFFT-optimal, with the first and last year of each song type. RevBayes FBD and BEAST2 SA are also compared on the `all` dataset, with all the years of each song type. Sequences have 5 states and all years of a song type share one sequence. | Model | Software | Tree prior | First and last year of a song type | |:---|:---|:---|:---| | **RevBayes FBD** | RevBayes 1.4.2 | Fossilized birth-death with sampled ancestors (`dnFBDP`) | Two separate samples | | **BEAST2 SA** | BEAST 2.7.7 (BEAST.base 2.7.8), SA 2.1.1 | Fossilized birth-death with sampled ancestors | Two separate samples | | **BEAST2 sRanges** | BEAST 2.7.7 (BEAST.base 2.7.8), SRanges 0.1.3 | Birth-death stratigraphic ranges | The two ends of one range | The rest of the model is shared: - **Substitution model**: GTR + gamma with 4 rate categories, 5 stationary frequencies and 10 exchangeability rates, both with flat Dirichlet priors, and an exponential prior (mean 1) on the gamma shape - **Clock**: relaxed, with branch rates drawn from an exponential distribution. Its mean has an exponential prior (mean 0.1) - **Tree prior**: exponential priors (mean 0.1) on the origination, loss and sampling rates, a uniform prior between 0 and 1000 years on the origin, and all songs in the last year sampled (rho = 1), conditioned on the origin time - **Gaps**: treated as missing data The models differ in three other ways: - **MCMC**: RevBayes uses 2 runs with 4 chains each, a burn-in of 50,000 generations and 150,000 generations after it. BEAST2 uses 2 independent replicates with a single chain, 50 million generations each, of which the first 10% are discarded - **Relaxed clock**: rates are continuous in RevBayes and take discrete categories in BEAST2 - **Tree moves**: the moves for sRanges are those enabled in the example of the package, without the jumps between tips and sampled ancestors or the exchange moves used in SA. The example flags some of these moves as pending review In sRanges the sequence of a song type is placed at both ends of its range, as in the examples of the package. The scripts are in `source/pilot_5ms/` and `source/pilot_5ms/beast2/`. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} taxa <- lapply(setNames(leks, leks), function(l) read.delim(file.path("./data/processed/pilot_5ms/taxa", paste0(l, "_5ms_bounds.tsv")))$taxon) song_type <- function(x) sub("-[0-9]{4}$", "", x) data.frame(lek = leks, taxa = lengths(taxa), song_types = sapply(taxa, function(x) length(unique(song_type(x)))), song_types_in_more_than_one_year = sapply(taxa, function(x) sum(table(song_type(x)) > 1))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
| |lek | taxa| song_types| song_types_in_more_than_one_year| |:---|:---|----:|----------:|--------------------------------:| |HC1 |HC1 | 9| 6| 3| |BR1 |BR1 | 17| 12| 5|
::: ::: # Convergence ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} read_log <- function(file) read.delim(file, comment.char = "#", check.names = FALSE) drop_burnin <- function(d) d[-seq_len(floor(nrow(d) * burnin)), ] rb_names <- c(likelihood = "Likelihood", origin = "origin_time", origination = "speciation_rate", loss = "extinction_rate", sampling = "psi", clock = "branch_rates_mean", alpha = "alpha_song") bt_names <- c(likelihood = "likelihood", origin = "origin", origination = "birth", loss = "death", sampling = "psi", clock = "clockMean", alpha = "alpha") par_labels <- c(likelihood = "Log likelihood", origin = "Origin age (years)", origination = "Song origination rate", loss = "Song loss rate", sampling = "Sampling rate (psi)", clock = "Mean rate of change", alpha = "Gamma shape") # same columns and names for all logs, including frequencies and exchangeability rates standardize <- function(d, names_map, sep) { er <- d[, grep(paste0("^er", sep), names(d))] sf <- d[, grep(paste0("^sf", sep), names(d))] out <- d[, unname(names_map)] names(out) <- names(names_map) names(er) <- paste0("er", seq_len(10)) names(sf) <- paste0("sf", seq_len(5)) cbind(out, er, sf) } rb_file <- function(lek, set, run) file.path(rb_dir, sprintf("%s_5ms_%s_run_%d.log", lek, set, run)) bt_file <- function(lek, model, seed) file.path(bt_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.%d.log", lek, model, seed)) read_runs <- function(lek) { r <- list() if (file.exists(rb_file(lek, "bounds", 2))) r[["RevBayes FBD"]] <- lapply(1:2, function(i) standardize(read_log(rb_file(lek, "bounds", i)), rb_names, "\\[")) r[["BEAST2 SA"]] <- lapply(c(101, 102), function(s) standardize(drop_burnin(read_log(bt_file(lek, "SA", s))), bt_names, "\\.")) r[["BEAST2 sRanges"]] <- lapply(c(101, 102), function(s) standardize(drop_burnin(read_log(bt_file(lek, "SR", s))), bt_names, "\\.")) if (file.exists(rb_file(lek, "all", 2))) r[["RevBayes FBD, all"]] <- lapply(1:2, function(i) standardize(read_log(rb_file(lek, "all", i)), rb_names, "\\[")) if (file.exists(bt_file(lek, "SA_all", 102))) r[["BEAST2 SA, all"]] <- lapply(c(101, 102), function(s) standardize(drop_burnin(read_log(bt_file(lek, "SA_all", s))), bt_names, "\\.")) r } runs <- lapply(setNames(leks, leks), read_runs) pooled <- lapply(runs, function(x) lapply(x, function(r) do.call(rbind, r))) available <- lapply(runs, function(x) intersect(models, names(x))) missing <- unlist(lapply(leks, function(l) if (!"RevBayes FBD" %in% available[[l]]) l)) ``` ::: Two independent runs of the same model should give the same results. We use the effective sample size (ESS, the smallest across parameters and runs) and the potential scale reduction factor (PSRF, the largest across parameters), which is close to 1 when the runs agree. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psrf <- function(a, b, p) { n <- min(nrow(a), nrow(b)) gelman.diag(mcmc.list(mcmc(a[[p]][seq_len(n)]), mcmc(b[[p]][seq_len(n)])), autoburnin = FALSE)$psrf[1] } convergence <- do.call(rbind, lapply(leks, function(l) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(runs[[l]]), function(m) { r <- runs[[l]][[m]] data.frame(lek = l, model = m, samples_per_run = nrow(r[[1]]), minimum_ESS = round(min(sapply(r, function(d) sapply(names(par_labels), function(p) effectiveSize(mcmc(d[[p]])))))), maximum_PSRF = round(max(sapply(names(par_labels), function(p) psrf(r[[1]], r[[2]], p))), 3)) })))) convergence ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|lek |model | samples_per_run| minimum_ESS| maximum_PSRF| |:---|:-----------------|---------------:|-----------:|------------:| |HC1 |RevBayes FBD | 1501| 1095| 1.005| |HC1 |BEAST2 SA | 4501| 4118| 1.002| |HC1 |BEAST2 sRanges | 4501| 4131| 1.001| |HC1 |RevBayes FBD, all | 1501| 1291| 1.005| |HC1 |BEAST2 SA, all | 4501| 3690| 1.001| |BR1 |RevBayes FBD | 1501| 1199| 1.002| |BR1 |BEAST2 SA | 4501| 3460| 1.001| |BR1 |BEAST2 sRanges | 4501| 3806| 1.000| |BR1 |RevBayes FBD, all | 1501| 1212| 1.002| |BR1 |BEAST2 SA, all | 4501| 3308| 1.000|
::: ::: All runs converged. # Parameters Medians with 95% intervals, combining both runs of each model. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ci <- function(x) sprintf("%.3g (%.3g to %.3g)", median(x), quantile(x, 0.025), quantile(x, 0.975)) med <- function(l, m, p) median(pooled[[l]][[m]][[p]]) rel <- function(l, a, b, p) round(100 * (med(l, b, p) / med(l, a, p) - 1)) par_table <- function(l) data.frame(parameter = unname(par_labels), sapply(available[[l]], function(m) sapply(names(par_labels), function(p) ci(pooled[[l]][[m]][[p]]))), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL) par_plot <- function(l) { d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(available[[l]], function(m) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(par_labels), function(p) { x <- pooled[[l]][[m]][[p]] data.frame(model = m, parameter = par_labels[[p]], median = median(x), low = quantile(x, 0.025), high = quantile(x, 0.975)) })))) d$model <- factor(d$model, rev(models)) d$parameter <- factor(d$parameter, par_labels) ggplot(d, aes(median, model)) + geom_linerange(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), linewidth = 0.7, color = "#408AB4") + geom_point(size = 2.8, color = "#408AB4") + facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) + labs(x = "Median and 95% interval", y = NULL) + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "gray92")) } ``` ::: ::: {.panel-tabset} ## HC1 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} par_table("HC1") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|parameter |RevBayes FBD |BEAST2 SA |BEAST2 sRanges | |:---------------------|:------------------------|:-----------------------|:-----------------------| |Log likelihood |-174 (-182 to -168) |-174 (-182 to -168) |-174 (-182 to -168) | |Origin age (years) |8.5 (4.35 to 20.6) |8.51 (4.38 to 20.3) |7.82 (4.06 to 18.7) | |Song origination rate |0.203 (0.0696 to 0.442) |0.208 (0.0765 to 0.46) |0.201 (0.0745 to 0.431) | |Song loss rate |0.153 (0.0431 to 0.394) |0.158 (0.0474 to 0.391) |0.147 (0.0422 to 0.358) | |Sampling rate (psi) |0.161 (0.055 to 0.368) |0.161 (0.0556 to 0.373) |0.208 (0.0707 to 0.495) | |Mean rate of change |0.0532 (0.0171 to 0.158) |0.052 (0.0174 to 0.152) |0.057 (0.0185 to 0.166) | |Gamma shape |2.22 (0.758 to 5.54) |2.13 (0.754 to 5.54) |2.13 (0.787 to 5.56) |

::: ```{.r .cell-code} par_plot("BR1") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](revbayes_beast2_comparison_files/figure-html/parameters BR1-1.png) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pars <- setdiff(names(par_labels), "likelihood") shift <- do.call(rbind, lapply(leks, function(l) { d <- data.frame(lek = l, parameter = unname(par_labels[pars]), sRanges_vs_SA = sapply(pars, function(p) sprintf("%+d%%", rel(l, "BEAST2 SA", "BEAST2 sRanges", p)))) d$SA_vs_RevBayes <- if ("RevBayes FBD" %in% available[[l]]) sapply(pars, function(p) sprintf("%+d%%", rel(l, "RevBayes FBD", "BEAST2 SA", p))) else "pending" d })) rownames(shift) <- NULL shift ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|lek |parameter |sRanges_vs_SA |SA_vs_RevBayes | |:---|:---------------------|:-------------|:--------------| |HC1 |Origin age (years) |-8% |+0% | |HC1 |Song origination rate |-4% |+3% | |HC1 |Song loss rate |-7% |+3% | |HC1 |Sampling rate (psi) |+30% |+0% | |HC1 |Mean rate of change |+10% |-2% | |HC1 |Gamma shape |+0% |-4% | |BR1 |Origin age (years) |-8% |+0% | |BR1 |Song origination rate |+30% |+1% | |BR1 |Song loss rate |+181% |+2% | |BR1 |Sampling rate (psi) |+13% |+0% | |BR1 |Mean rate of change |+3% |-2% | |BR1 |Gamma shape |-1% |-4% |
::: ::: Differences between medians. BEAST2 SA reproduces RevBayes when both are available. sRanges changes the parameters of the tree prior more in BR1 than in HC1: in BR1 it has a higher song loss rate (+181%) and origination rate (+30%), although intervals overlap. Parameters of song change (mean rate of change and gamma shape) are similar in all models. Intervals are wide, so the priors probably contribute to these estimates. # Trees ## Comparing trees between models The two models represent persisting song types differently. With sampled ancestors, the first year of a song type can be the direct ancestor of other song types, so its two years do not necessarily form a clade. With stratigraphic ranges, both years belong to one lineage. Comparing clades of individual taxa would therefore mix real differences with differences in representation. We compare clades at the level of **song types**: each clade is the set of song types below a node, counting a song type when any of its years is there. Support is the proportion of trees with that set, out of 1500 trees per run. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} read_rb_trees <- function(lek, run, set = "bounds") { d <- read_log(file.path(rb_dir, sprintf("%s_5ms_%s_run_%d.trees", lek, set, run))) s <- d[[ncol(d)]] lapply(s[round(seq(1, length(s), length.out = n_trees))], function(t) read.tree(text = t)) } read_bt_trees <- function(lek, model, seed) { x <- read.nexus(file.path(bt_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.%d.trees", lek, model, seed))) x <- x[-seq_len(floor(length(x) * burnin))] x <- x[round(seq(1, length(x), length.out = n_trees))] lapply(seq_along(x), function(i) x[[i]]) } # clades as sets of song types, without single song types or all of them type_clades <- function(trees) { counts <- list() for (tr in trees) { tr <- collapse.singles(tr) types <- song_type(tr$tip.label) n_types <- length(unique(types)) parts <- prop.part(tr) keys <- unique(vapply(parts, function(p) paste(sort(unique(types[p])), collapse = " "), "")) size <- lengths(strsplit(keys, " ")) for (k in keys[size > 1 & size < n_types]) counts[[k]] <- (if (is.null(counts[[k]])) 0 else counts[[k]]) + 1 } unlist(counts) / length(trees) } clade_table <- lapply(setNames(leks, leks), function(l) { sets <- list("BEAST2 SA 1" = read_bt_trees(l, "SA", 101), "BEAST2 SA 2" = read_bt_trees(l, "SA", 102), "BEAST2 sRanges 1" = read_bt_trees(l, "SR", 101), "BEAST2 sRanges 2" = read_bt_trees(l, "SR", 102)) if ("RevBayes FBD" %in% available[[l]]) sets <- c(list("RevBayes FBD 1" = read_rb_trees(l, 1), "RevBayes FBD 2" = read_rb_trees(l, 2)), sets) support <- lapply(sets, type_clades) all_clades <- unique(unlist(lapply(support, names))) m <- sapply(support, function(x) { v <- x[all_clades]; v[is.na(v)] <- 0; v }) rownames(m) <- gsub(paste0(l, "-"), "", all_clades) m }) mean_support <- lapply(clade_table, function(m) { out <- data.frame(row.names = rownames(m)) for (mod in models) { k <- grep(paste0("^", mod, " [12]$"), colnames(m)); if (length(k)) out[[mod]] <- rowMeans(m[, k, drop = FALSE]) } out }) ``` ::: ## Agreement ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} agreement <- function(l, a, b) { m <- clade_table[[l]] if (!all(c(a, b) %in% colnames(m))) return(NULL) data.frame(lek = l, comparison = paste(a, "vs", b), correlation = round(cor(m[, a], m[, b]), 3), largest_difference = round(max(abs(m[, a] - m[, b])), 2)) } do.call(rbind, lapply(leks, function(l) rbind( agreement(l, "RevBayes FBD 1", "RevBayes FBD 2"), agreement(l, "BEAST2 SA 1", "BEAST2 SA 2"), agreement(l, "BEAST2 sRanges 1", "BEAST2 sRanges 2"), agreement(l, "RevBayes FBD 1", "BEAST2 SA 1"), agreement(l, "BEAST2 SA 1", "BEAST2 sRanges 1"), agreement(l, "BEAST2 SA 2", "BEAST2 sRanges 2")))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}
|lek |comparison | correlation| largest_difference| |:---|:------------------------------------|-----------:|------------------:| |HC1 |RevBayes FBD 1 vs RevBayes FBD 2 | 0.998| 0.03| |HC1 |BEAST2 SA 1 vs BEAST2 SA 2 | 0.999| 0.02| |HC1 |BEAST2 sRanges 1 vs BEAST2 sRanges 2 | 0.998| 0.03| |HC1 |RevBayes FBD 1 vs BEAST2 SA 1 | 0.999| 0.02| |HC1 |BEAST2 SA 1 vs BEAST2 sRanges 1 | 0.999| 0.02| |HC1 |BEAST2 SA 2 vs BEAST2 sRanges 2 | 0.999| 0.03| |BR1 |RevBayes FBD 1 vs RevBayes FBD 2 | 0.999| 0.03| |BR1 |BEAST2 SA 1 vs BEAST2 SA 2 | 0.998| 0.06| |BR1 |BEAST2 sRanges 1 vs BEAST2 sRanges 2 | 0.998| 0.03| |BR1 |RevBayes FBD 1 vs BEAST2 SA 1 | 0.997| 0.07| |BR1 |BEAST2 SA 1 vs BEAST2 sRanges 1 | 0.839| 0.61| |BR1 |BEAST2 SA 2 vs BEAST2 sRanges 2 | 0.837| 0.62|
::: ::: Replicates of the same model agree in all cases, so differences between models are not due to a lack of convergence. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} support_plot <- do.call(rbind, lapply(leks, function(l) { s <- mean_support[[l]] out <- data.frame(lek = l, x = s[["BEAST2 SA"]], y = s[["BEAST2 sRanges"]], panel = "BEAST2 sRanges") if (!is.null(s[["RevBayes FBD"]])) out <- rbind(out, data.frame(lek = l, x = s[["BEAST2 SA"]], y = s[["RevBayes FBD"]], panel = "RevBayes FBD")) out })) support_plot$lek <- factor(support_plot$lek, leks) ggplot(support_plot, aes(x, y)) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "gray70") + geom_point(size = 2.2, color = "#408AB4", alpha = 0.7) + facet_grid(lek ~ panel) + coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) + labs(x = "Clade support in BEAST2 SA", y = "Clade support in the other model") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](revbayes_beast2_comparison_files/figure-html/support plot-1.png) ::: ::: Each point is a clade of song types, and the line marks equal support. ## Supported clades Clades with at least 20% support in any model, ordered by their largest support: ::: {.panel-tabset} ## HC1 |clade | RevBayes FBD| BEAST2 SA| BEAST2 sRanges| |:-----------|------------:|---------:|--------------:| |C4 K1 M1 | 0.66| 0.67| 0.67| |C4 K1 | 0.45| 0.46| 0.46| |K2 K3 | 0.43| 0.42| 0.42| |K2 K3 L1 | 0.43| 0.42| 0.42| |K2 L1 | 0.35| 0.36| 0.35| |C4 K1 L1 M1 | 0.33| 0.33| 0.32| |K1 M1 | 0.19| 0.21| 0.20| |C4 M1 | 0.21| 0.20| 0.21| ## BR1 |clade | RevBayes FBD| BEAST2 SA| BEAST2 sRanges| |:--------------------|------------:|---------:|--------------:| |A2 E2 F1 | 1.00| 0.99| 1.00| |A2 C1 C2 E2 F1 | 0.79| 0.78| 0.52| |D1 E3 | 0.69| 0.69| 0.07| |A1 D1 D2 D3 D4 E1 E3 | 0.66| 0.66| 0.36| |C1 C2 | 0.64| 0.64| 0.40| |A2 E2 | 0.52| 0.50| 0.50| |A2 C1 C2 E2 E3 F1 | 0.16| 0.17| 0.49| |A1 D4 | 0.48| 0.43| 0.26| |D4 E1 | 0.43| 0.47| 0.30| |D3 E1 | 0.45| 0.41| 0.22| |A1 D3 | 0.40| 0.44| 0.18| |A1 D1 D2 D3 D4 E1 | 0.18| 0.19| 0.43| |E2 F1 | 0.28| 0.29| 0.29| |D1 D3 | 0.03| 0.03| 0.27| |A2 F1 | 0.20| 0.20| 0.21| |D1 D3 E1 | 0.20| 0.16| 0.12| |C2 E3 | 0.06| 0.06| 0.20| ::: ::: {.cell} ::: In HC1, the models support the same clades of song types. In BR1, sRanges changes them: the largest drop is for {D1 E3} (from 0.69 with SA to 0.07 with sRanges), and the largest increase for {A2 C1 C2 E2 E3 F1} (from 0.17 to 0.49). SA supports 6 clades with more than 50% support and sRanges 3. ## Interpreting the sRanges results - **Not a convergence problem**: the two sRanges runs agree with each other as closely as the SA runs do - **Rates of song change are unaffected**: the mean rate of change and the gamma shape are similar in all models, so ranges affect the tree prior (origination, loss and sampling) more than the evolution of the sequences - **More persisting song types in BR1**: BR1 has more song types recorded in more than one year than HC1, which may explain why ranges matter more there Ranges are closer to what a song type is (one song that persists in the lek), but the results come with caveats: - **Tree moves**: sRanges has fewer tree moves than SA (no jumps between tips and sampled ancestors, no exchange moves), and its own example flags some of them as pending review. Agreement between replicates does not rule out that the moves affect the results - **Maturity**: version 0.1.3, not listed in the BEAST2 package manager, so it was installed by hand. RevBayes 1.4.2 has no equivalent model (`dnFBDRP` was removed), so it cannot be cross-checked in another program - **Fit not tested**: we have not compared the marginal likelihood of sRanges and SA, which would show which model the data favor - **Only one dataset**: ranges only use the first and last year (`bounds`), so they cannot be applied to the `all` dataset # RevBayes and BEAST2 with the same model RevBayes FBD and BEAST2 SA implement the same model, so they should give the same results with both datasets. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pairs <- list(bounds = c("RevBayes FBD", "BEAST2 SA"), all = c("RevBayes FBD, all", "BEAST2 SA, all")) equivalence <- do.call(rbind, lapply(leks, function(l) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pairs), function(ds) { m <- pairs[[ds]] if (!all(m %in% names(pooled[[l]]))) return(NULL) do.call(rbind, lapply(pars, function(p) data.frame(lek = l, dataset = ds, parameter = par_labels[[p]], RevBayes = ci(pooled[[l]][[m[1]]][[p]]), BEAST2_SA = ci(pooled[[l]][[m[2]]][[p]]), difference = 100 * (median(pooled[[l]][[m[2]]][[p]]) / median(pooled[[l]][[m[1]]][[p]]) - 1)))) })))) rownames(equivalence) <- NULL data.frame(equivalence[, 1:5], difference = sprintf("%+.0f%%", equivalence$difference)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

They do not lead to the same trees, so the topology depends on how persistence is modelled. # Marginal likelihood: global vs relaxed clock The first version of the study chose the clock model with marginal likelihoods (stepping stone and path sampling in RevBayes). Here the same comparison is run in both programs, for both leks and datasets, with the FBD (SA) tree prior: - **RevBayes**: `powerPosterior` with the settings of the first version: 100 powers, 5,000 generations of pre-burnin and 2,000 generations per power (RevBayes 1.4.2 adds 2,000 generations of pre-burnin per power and discards the first 25%) - **BEAST2**: path sampler of the MODEL_SELECTION package (1.6.2) with 100 steps, 1.2 million states per step (60% discarded) and 1.5 million states of pre-burnin. This is about the same number of proposals per power as RevBayes (281 moves per generation in HC1 `bounds`) - **Powers**: in both, quantiles of a Beta(0.2, 1) distribution - **Relaxed clock in BEAST2**: continuous branch rates with an exponential prior, as in RevBayes. The rate categories of the BEAST2 runs above have no prior term, which leaves the posterior unchanged but would inflate the marginal likelihood by about *n* log(*n*) for *n* branches - **Replicates**: 3 per model and program, with different seeds Stepping stone (Xie et al. 2011) and path sampling are computed with the same code for both programs, from the log-likelihood samples at each power (`source/pilot_5ms/ml/summarise_ml.R`). For RevBayes this reproduces the estimates printed by RevBayes. The estimate printed by the BEAST2 path sampler is not used: it is 37 to 48 log units lower than what its own samples give. The scripts are in `source/pilot_5ms/ml/`. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ml <- read.csv("./output/pilot_5ms/ml/ml_estimates.csv") ml$program <- factor(ml$program, levels = c("RevBayes", "BEAST2")) ml$dataset <- factor(ml$dataset, levels = c("bounds", "all")) ml$lek <- factor(ml$lek, levels = leks) msd <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f ± %.1f", mean(x), sd(x)) ml_table <- aggregate(stepping_stone ~ lek + dataset + program + clock, ml, msd) ml_table <- reshape(ml_table, idvar = c("lek", "dataset", "program"), timevar = "clock", direction = "wide") names(ml_table) <- sub("stepping_stone.", "", names(ml_table)) # Bayes factors (relaxed minus global), with all combinations of replicates bf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ml, list(ml$lek, ml$dataset, ml$program), drop = TRUE), function(x) { d <- outer(x$stepping_stone[x$clock == "relaxed"], x$stepping_stone[x$clock == "global"], "-") data.frame(lek = x$lek[1], dataset = x$dataset[1], program = x$program[1], log_BF = mean(d), min = min(d), max = max(d)) })) ml_table <- merge(ml_table, bf, sort = FALSE) ml_table <- ml_table[order(ml_table$lek, ml_table$dataset, ml_table$program), ] rownames(ml_table) <- NULL data.frame(ml_table[, c("lek", "dataset", "program", "global", "relaxed")], log_BF = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", ml_table$log_BF, ml_table$min, ml_table$max)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

In the MCMC, RevBayes runs 2 runs of 4 chains each in parallel, while BEAST2 runs 2 independent single-chain replicates. ## Pros and cons | | RevBayes (FBD) | BEAST2 (SA) | BEAST2 (sRanges) | |:---|:---|:---|:---| | **Results** | Reference | Same as RevBayes | Different trees and rates in BR1 | | **Song types as persisting lineages** | No: two separate samples | No: two separate samples | **Yes**: one range per song type | | **MCMC speed** | Slower (1 to 2 h with 8 cores) | **Faster** (20 to 45 min with 1 core) | **Faster** (similar to SA) | | **Marginal likelihood** | **Built in and reliable** | Possible, but must be computed from the saved samples | Not tested | | **Posterior predictive tests (P3)** | **Built in** (used in the first version) | Not available; would need our own simulation | Not available | | **Maturity** | **Used in the first version, well documented** | **Well established** | Early version (0.1.3), installed by hand | | **Tree moves** | **Full set** | **Full set** | Reduced, some pending review | | **Datasets** | `all` and `bounds` | `all` and `bounds` | `bounds` only | | **Setup** | **Existing scripts**; RevBayes 1.4.2 needs `dnFBDP` and an `age` column in the taxon file | XML files written from R | XML files written from R, more manual setup | | **Collaboration** | **Familiar to the coauthors** (Beatriz runs it) | New to the project | New to the project | ## Options 1. **Stay with RevBayes (recommended)**: same design as the first version, with built-in marginal likelihoods and P3. Report BEAST2 SA as an independent validation on HC1 and BR1 2. **Add sRanges as a sensitivity analysis**: run it on the `bounds` datasets in BEAST2 and report whether treating song types as ranges changes the conclusions. Before this, compare the fit of sRanges and SA with marginal likelihoods, and check its tree moves (for example, by sampling from the prior and comparing with the expected distribution) 3. **Move everything to BEAST2**: faster, and it gives access to sRanges, but marginal likelihoods need our own estimator and P3 would have to be built and validated from scratch ## Still to test -
